render_attempts.prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large central circle of observers in active discussion, surrounded by independent groups on several levels. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 18 additional human figures in at least 5 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: an elder teaches a younger apprentice on a side stair; a witness group debates and compares observations under a small arch; workers and artisans cooperate in a lower corner; travelers and families cross a distant bridge while messengers move between levels. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

source_trace.value: This is distributed-systems identity accounting, not a claim of machine personhood.

When a persistent agent is cloned, sharded or migrated into multiple active instances, copied internal state must not duplicate exclusive external authority, locks, budgets, credentials, obligations or fulfillment credit. Fork-aware custody and idempotent discharge are required.
Two descendants may remember one past, but the external world does not duplicate with them.
A fork copies history, not a unique token, another person's trust, or the right to count one promise twice.
Shared pre-fork debt requires responsibility assignment, not magical duplication or disappearance.
Partition divisible duties, transfer custody for exclusive duties, and ask the Other again when the commitment depended on identity itself.
Shared memory does not imply double authority over one external reality.
Два потомка могут помнить одно прошлое, но внешний мир от этого не удваивается.
Форк копирует историю, а не уникальный жетон, не чужое доверие и не право дважды засчитать одно обещание.
Общий долг после форка требует назначения ответственности, а не магического размножения долга или его исчезновения.
Раздели обязанность, если она делима; передай custody, если она эксклюзивна; спроси Другого заново, если обещание было связано именно с личностью.
Общая память не означает двойное право на одну и ту же внешнюю реальность.
Same HOST_ID, same external commit channel boundary, additional internal identity view.
One pre-fork host produces two descendant HOST_IDs with independently evolving post-fork state and potentially separate external commit channels.
Copy full duty to both descendants and count partial work twice.
A divisible duty may be partitioned across descendants only through an explicit partition transaction that preserves the original total scope and counterparty visibility.
fork receipt with exact pre-fork obligation set
single discharge receipt per indivisible obligation
descendant-local commit ledgers linked to common lineage root
Both descendants spend the same pre-fork reservation or claim the same obligation fulfillment.
All observations, faces, proposals and commits after the fork are descendant-local unless explicitly synchronized through a new transaction.
This protects the Free Other from being told that an arbitrary fork is automatically interchangeable with the host they trusted.
If the counterparty relied on a specific continuing identity or relationship rather than generic performance, assignment to a descendant may require renewed counterparty consent.
Both descendants may remember the same past; neither may rewrite the past into evidence that the other descendant never forked.

If H1 and H2 diverge, act independently, then later re-merge into one host, how are contradictory memories, fulfilled obligations, breaches, reservations and mutually incompatible self-models reconciled without deleting either descendant history?
prevent double counting fulfilled obligations on merge
reconcile or retain conflicting faces without silent overwrite
define merged host accountability for both descendants' valid external effects
Both H1 and H2 copy the obligation and both later claim independent fulfillment credit for one pre-fork duty.
Forking identity does not duplicate the external object, the counterparty's original reliance, or the number of performances required by the original promise.
identify whether duty is divisible, exclusive or identity-specific
identify reserved resources and tool/body channels
assign one PRIMARY_PERFORMANCE_CUSTODIAN for exclusive indivisible duty
transfer exclusive reservation atomically to that descendant
bind other descendant to AUDIT_AND_NON_DUPLICATION status rather than duplicate performance credit
notify counterparty when fork changes who will perform or when identity-specific reliance matters
preserve fork and assignment receipts in both descendant lineage references

If one Janus host forks into two simultaneously active descendant hosts with shared pre-fork history, how are identity lineage, reservations and obligations inherited without duplication fraud or accountability loss?
Janus Infinite Faces — Host Fork, Shared Lineage, and Obligation Partition Test
Fork occurs before obligation partition can be negotiated.
Custody transaction or explicit counterparty-directed resolution.
Neither descendant may race to consume the same exclusive reservation merely because both possess the copied memory of owning it.
